topic: Memory Hierarchy and Caching Strategies: With Disk
explanation: The memory hierarchy mitigates the CPU-memory performance gap by organizing storage into tiers of increasing latency and capacity, ranging from CPU registers to L1/L2/L3 caches, main memory (DRAM), and persistent storage (Disk/SSD). Caching strategies exploit temporal and spatial locality by moving frequently accessed data blocks closer to the CPU, primarily into SRAM-based cache levels. Effective caching minimizes average memory access time (AMAT) by maximizing the hit rate in faster tiers, thereby reducing reliance on high-latency disk I/O for data retrieval. This multi-level approach ensures the processor operates efficiently despite the physical limitations of large-scale, high-speed memory.
